GitHub Copilot app: turn a fragile code path into a test brief.

What changed: at Universe 2026, GitHub introduced an app connecting agents and tools across projects.

What it does: it brings the work into one surface. In GitHub's November 3 Arnis profile, Louis Erbkamm describes using sub-agents to inspect sensitive areas and suggest regression cases. He still reviews every pull request.

Builder value: the things you keep checking by hand can become explicit instructions, rather than knowledge that stays in your head.

Try this week on a repo you can access:
Choose one draft pull request and one fragile behavior. Ask Copilot: "Inspect this path. Propose three failure cases and a test for each. Do not edit files yet."
Review the plan, then authorize the smallest useful test change. Run the tests and inspect the diff before merging.

That echoes our latest Tech Thursday discussion: break the role into tasks, then decide which task AI should handle. A proposed workflow, not a claim that we ran this exact experiment on stream.

The signal: prompts are becoming reviewable work. Your judgment still decides what ships.

Save this for your next pull request.

text:
AI video storyboard: six stills can plan five transitions.

In our latest Tech Thursday walkthrough, the host asked ChatGPT for six frames using a face reference and an environment reference. The story moved from an office into his Layer8 lab.

The reusable part is the planning math: adjacent pairs give you five planned transitions, not a guarantee of five usable clips.

1. Write one sentence describing the change.
2. Define all six stills before animating.
3. Keep the subject and environment references consistent.
4. Test one adjacent pair before batching the rest.
5. Review the joins, then assemble only the clips that work.

The stream also showed a third-clip block. Treat a block as a stop-and-review checkpoint, not something to bypass. A model recommendation isn't a production guarantee.

This is a storyboard method, not a claim that every video tool supports start-and-end frames. Check your chosen tool's controls first.

Save this before your next AI video build.
